the set of actual and potential buyers of a product
the steps from understanding the market to capturing value from customers
the process of identifying customer needs and satisfying them profitably through exchange
items.s: Transaction: a trade of values between two parties, such as money for goods. The other options describe Marketing process, Marketing, Market.

items.q: In this course, Cognitive dissonance refers to
o: the doubt a buyer feels after a purchase that the choice may have been wrong
the stage in which a buyer settles on the product and seller to use
the stage in which a buyer looks for facts about possible solutions
what a buyer feels and does after the purchase, including satisfaction or regret
items.s: Cognitive dissonance: the doubt a buyer feels after a purchase that the choice may have been wrong. The other options describe Purchase decision, Information search, Post-purchase behaviour.

items.q: The correct meaning of Marketing concept is
o: keeping existing customers buying through continuing satisfaction and attention
the belief that buyers prefer products that are cheap and widely available
the belief that success comes from meeting target customer needs better than rivals
the belief that marketing should balance customer wants, company profit and public welfare
items.s: Marketing concept: the belief that success comes from meeting target customer needs better than rivals. The other options describe Customer retention, Production concept, Societal marketing concept.
